newsitem.title: INDIA: India HPCL to convert warrants to shares.
newsitem.headline: India HPCL to convert warrants to shares.

text.p: India's state-run refiner Hindustan Petroleum Corp Ltd (HPCL) on Wednesday released a notice for conversion of warrants into equity shares to raise 5.9 billion rupees.
The following are the salient features of the issue opening on February 24 and closing on March 25.
+ Each detachable warrant will be converted into a equity share at a price of 340 rupees per share.
+ The amount will be payable in four instalments of 85 rupees each payable over a period of one year.
+ Holders will have the following options - to renounce the entitlement, to apply for additional shares in multiples of 100 or to apply for split of entitlement in multiples of 100 shares.
The notice for conversion of detachable, tradeable warrants is in accordance with terms of the prospectus for initial public offer issued in January 1995.
After the conversion of warrants into equity, the paid up capital will rise to about 2.26 billion rupees from 2.08 billion at present, C. Ramulu, executive director told reporters.
After the conversion, Indian government's holdings in HPCL would fall to 51 percent from 55.3 percent now, Ramulu said.
Indian financial institutions and banks now hold 29.40 percent, foreign institutional investors and expatriate Indians hold 5.7 percent, employees 2.3 percent and others 7.3 percent.
HPCL is India's second largest refiner and is the country's most actively traded petroleum stock.
HPCL's market capitalisation accounts for about 5.0 percent of the 30-share Bombay Stock Exchange sensitive index, Ramulu said. HPCL has a market capitalisation of 80.0 billion rupees.
